posts.cooked:
One of the recurring themes of the post-Oblivaeon timelines, as mentioned in the Letters Page a lot, is that with Oblivaeon gone, reality is no longer fracturing--and that the reality-fracturing encountered within the Sentinels of the Multiverse card game was what enabled travel across time, jumping between probabilistic worldtracks (OK, OK, I'm putting Anathem down now, I promise), and the like.

Does this mean that time travel and parallel realities are somehow verboten within the "Tactics Timeline" and "RPG TImeline" (for lack of a better set of monikers)?

Of course, if I wanted to, as the GM of a Sentinel Comics RPG session, I could easily say "you're in SIlver Gulch now, it's 1884--or indeed 1882" as easily as I could say "you're the Freedom Five, and it's time to play through the Vengeance Event," but as a matter of "the official rules" of the universe(s), are time travel stories and parallel-reality stories off limits to the Two Timelines? Or is it just that they are, effectively, isolated from each other, so there's no way to cross between them? Even if members of those timelines go back in time or to parallel realities, those are "localized" around their branch of the split, and never the twain shall meet? (Which again doesn't stop me as a GM from saying "you're going to meet the Freedom Six when you get transported to a place called Broken City, which looks familiar and yet not," but you know what I mean.)

The way I understand it, it's kind of like a funnel with two spouts.

Up until OblivAeon, crossing into realities was easy, as each swirled together.  Try to go back 'up' the funnel by time-traveling, and you really just ended up in a different stream, still heading down the funnel towards OblivAeon.

OblivAeon, naturally, is the apex of the funnel:  all of time and reality pours towards that single point.

After OblivAeon, all of time and reality goes in one of two directions: RPG-ward or Tactics-ward.  And, just as you can't 'pour up' the funnel, you can't time-travel past OblivAeon (or, really, even at all).

Haka spoilers:  In my mind, the "core card game reality" Haka heads through the Mistgate in search of other heroes, ending up marooned in the Tactics timeline.  Meanwhile, his alternate-reality female counterpart takes on the role of Haka in the RPG-reality.  Together, the two make up the "final pair" of Hakas which make each other effectively immortal.

Just my 2 cents.

It was me who mentioned that in the Starter Kit Argent Adept mentioned that the Prime Wardens broke up after the loss of Haka. He's caring for Akash'Flora and it seems part of the Starter Kit story is getting the Prime Wardens back together again, to deal with some new threat. IT involved SPider-Bots that used a lot of different tech. And by a lot of different tech I mean tech from every major source that I am aware of. Bunker, Tachyon, Unity, Omnitron, Baron Blade, Voss, FILTER, and I think Revocorp if memory serves me.

 

We also know that part of getting the team together is going to involve the Femae version of HAka fighting Tempest. And Tempest doesn't rejoin, perhaps only if she joins but that seems signifigant. But it was almost mentioned in passing by our DM so it is hard to know for certain how much is revealed in the Starter Kit.

 

As for not actually breaking the "no dimension hopping rule" it is very possible that you are right, but wouldn't it be odd for Haka to lay low for 5+ years in the tactics timeline, allowing so many people to be injured and hurt in the events that follow, without showing up on anyones radar?

 

We know he isn't in Broken City, and if we take their original production schedule as the timeline for Tactics it is quite a long while before Prime War and Haka showing up. It seems exceedingly strange to me that he would just be laying low and not doing anything of importance. That isn't Haka.

 

 

cnranger:

 Or maybe the mist gate spit him out at exactly the Prime War arc skipping over the time difference?

 

That's an interesting idea. We do know there is this Mist in the Tactics Timeline that is making things vanish and disappear.

 

Let us assume that the Gates are more built like tunnels. There is a section where you are in neither reality, but instead between them. Haka is mid-journey, or trying to run and jump back thru the Gate when it closes. He's smashed in the middle where he is between realities instead of in any single reality.

 

Most people would die, but Haka is "quantumly entangled" or however you would phrase it, and cannot die as long as his counter part is still alive and therefore he is simply floating and existing between realities.

 

Eventually, when someone tries something new to combat this mist, it results in Haka getting spit out into the Tactics timeline, right in time for Prime War. This works as well as a narrative retcon, Haka was lost and "gotten rid of" by the writers of the RPG timeline, but the Tactics writers found a way to bring him back for ther story that does not break any of the new rules, just bends them in half.

 

I like it. Headcannon for now until disproven or displaced.

 

scifantasy:

But as a matter of "the canonical story," what's the status?This is turning into a specific question for the podcast…

 

Only two people have ever traveled directly in time in the Sentinels of the Multiverse Story. Chrono-Ranger and La Capitan/Commodora. Everyone else reality hopped.

 

Officially, reality hopping is no longer possible, because that was only possible because of Oblivaeon and Oblivaeon no longer exists in a capacity that allows for that to happen. That is the canon answer as far as we the consumers have been told.

 

As for Time Travel, Chrono-Ranger can no longer travel like he used to. And instead works with manipulating Time and traveling in short bursts, like no more than an hour or so, as far as I understand from the future section of Chrono-Ranger.

 

I do not know the fate of La Comodora or La Capitan, so I cannot comment.

 

However, since what they were doing is seperate from traveling to different realities, it is reasonable to assume that time travel is possible. However, it would be incredibly risky and perhaps locked down by some force. Because, if it is possible to jump back in time the Oblivaeon fight could be affected. A change could end up turning the fight at a crucial moment and allowing Oblivaeon to win, which would cause massive problems for the Multiverse if it were to happen.

 

This is actually a good spot for La Commodora, acting as the Gate Keeper for Time. Preventing or closely monitoring anyone who might travel back to before Oblivaeon so that the timeline is not disrupted and the events unfold like they are supposed to.

 

Or, because of the Death of Oblivaeon and it itself probably becoming a massive fixed point in time, it might have become impossible to travel back before that. There is simply too much chronal interference and energy released during that battle that it would be like taking a sailboat thru the Red Spot of Jupiter, you'll be smashed to pieces and killed nearly instantly, so it is a really really bad idea.

 

Not sure which of these ideas I prefer.

 But it was almost mentioned in passing by our DM so it is hard to know for certain how much is revealed in the Starter Kit. As for not actually breaking the "no dimension hopping rule" it is very possible that you are right, but wouldn't it be odd for Haka to lay low for 5+ years in the tactics timeline, allowing so many people to be injured and hurt in the events that follow, without showing up on anyones radar? We know he isn't in Broken City, and if we take their original production schedule as the timeline for Tactics it is quite a long while before Prime War and Haka showing up. It seems exceedingly strange to me that he would just be laying low and not doing anything of importance. That isn't Haka.  
[/quote]
 

From my POV it sounds exactly like Haka, he probably realised the state the world was in and wandered around to help fix things in areas most of the world forgot, Oblivaeon's attack on Earth probably caused massive widespread damage not just in places we know, whilst places like Megaopolis probably received massive amounts of public and private funding to fix the damage what about places in Africa, China, New Zealand...

Haka is the sort who sees violence as a last resort, and would relish a chance to use his strength and ability to take large amounts of damage to help people, like helping at underfunded construction sites carrying stuff and doing the more dangerous work to prevent others from hurting themselves.  He probably only shows up for Prime War because Argent Adept sought him out to help.

I hope I'm not coming across as argumenative, but I love back and forths like this.

 

Haka always has his Ta Moko period. They are tatoos that he took a lot of effort to make, and he does not need to reapply them. But, personality is a lot. He's probably terrifying in combat, which is not how he presents himself out of it. Still, He is unnatural large and has distinctive facial tatoos, there is little hiding who he is, and he doesn't put much effort into trying to hide it. It all depends on how famous Haka is in a given area at the time.

 

 

Paul is a completely different story. He is famous. Everyone knows that Paul Parsons is Legacy. His Father and Grandfather were famous in the wars, he's famous, he's married to (if memory serves me) a US Senator. Every aspect of his life leads to him being incredibly well known, and it has been indicated that he has no secret identity. He's never tried to hide who or what he is, so everyone knows it… at least anyone who bothers to pay attention.

posts.name: Arcanist Lupus
posts.cooked:
Also, it's worth noting that in Tactics the public opinion of heroes is rather low.  They're no longer being met with parades and confetti.  Now, Haka has a lot of practice being disarming with unfriendly/suspicious strangers, so I don't think the negative attitudes will be much of a problem for him.  But it means that the towns and villages that he visits are going to be less inclined to brag about his presence.

And that's even if they can.  There are a lot of people in the world who still don't have internet access.  We think of the modern world as having instant communications to every location, but that's not always true in the poorer regions.  And that's in our world, which hasn't just fought a world-spanning war against the apocalypse.  And I think that it's a reasonable bet that those poorer regions are where Haka will be spending most of his time.  

Sure, anyone who really wanted to track Haka down probably could.  But the world is still rebuilding from near destruction - everybody has better things to do.

You might need to revise your lore on that element. This comes from his bio and shows precedent of his Ta Moko disapearing:

However, Aata’s great power is what eventually laid him low, bringing his reign to an end. One morning, after the night of a great battle, his Tā Moko, the facial tattoos identifying him as a Maori warrior, faded completely. Though they knew not what Aata could have done to displease their gods so thoroughly, they took it as a sign that their once great chief had been cursed. Aata’s own right hand man, Ruru, stepped up to challenge him in order to cleanse their village of his taint. Outwitting the giant warrior, still stunned from his tribe turning against him, Ruru dealt Aata a killing blow. Ruru dragged his former friend’s body into the desert, slit his throat, and left him to the dogs.

So it has been clearly established that his immortality can cause it to heal and disapear. He's also shown without it on the picture of the FV BBQ. If I remember well the quote on Ta Moko also supports this.

Yeah, what Powerhound said. The Letter's Page told us he only needed to reapply them once, but it was incredibly grueling and painful.

 

 

I do agree with Arcanist Lupus, it is still possible to disappear into the world. Like I said, I'm used to considering all the heroes to be super famous, but Haka while recognizable would be one of the less recognizable heroes simply because he's a quiet guy who disappears a lot.

 

I'm convince that he could have gone off into the mists of the world, tending to the poorest sections of the world during the five years before Tactics starts and even however long it took to get to Prime War.

 

I am not convinced that is what the actual story is going to be though. There seemed to be hints in the Letters PAge that Haka showing up was a bit more than that.

 

So, Possible, yes, but I think when we get the story of Haka entering Prime War we are going to be getting a much different story from him.
